info.title: Victual REST API
info.description:
Authentication is done via API keys (header *VICTUAL-API-KEY* or same named query parameter), which you can manage [here](PlaceHolderManageApiKeysUrl).
Additionally requests from within the frontend are also valid (via session cookie).

**Dates and times.** Every instant this API stores or sends is RFC 3339 in UTC with exactly six fractional digits - `2026-10-04T18:30:00.000000Z` - typed *format: date-time* (ADR-0027 decision 2, issue #650). The fixed width is part of the contract: text order is chronological order, so two values may be compared as strings. The one exception is *time_local* on the system time endpoint, the same instant with the server's offset (`2026-10-04T14:30:00.000000-04:00`). Fields whose column is a SQL DATE are calendar dates, typed *format: date* and written `YYYY-MM-DD`; they are never converted between zones. Days the server computes - due today, overdue, expiring in N days - are days in the server's configured time zone. A value sent without an offset - to the three write fields *tracked_time* and *done_time*, to a generic entity write, or as a `query[]` comparison - is a wall clock in the server's configured zone: a repeated hour names the earlier instant, and a skipped hour is refused with **400**. Send an offset to name any instant unambiguously. These values were local wall clocks in the server's zone, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, until migration 0301 converted them.

schema.description:
One element per row of the requested entity. The union is **undiscriminated** - the entity is in the path, not in the payload - so a generated client decodes it by trying each member and keeping the first that validates. Each member therefore declares `required` properties that no other member has. Before that, `Product` had no required properties and so matched any JSON object, and every row of every entity decoded as a Product: `quantity_units` lost `name_plural`, `locations` lost `parent_location_id`. Issue #232.

**A row of a listable entity that has no schema here matches no member and will not decode.** That is deliberate - a loud failure in place of the silent wrong answer it replaces. `ExposedEntity_NotIncludingNotListable` names every entity this route serves and only the ten below are described; the rest are undocumented rather than absent, and a client that needs one should read this route outside its generated code until a schema exists.

A flagged self-edit sent no new password, or one identical to the current one. first_name, last_name, password, current_password or picture_file_name was present and not a string. See this operation's own description for exactly when each applies.

put.description:
Requires USERS_EDIT to edit another user, or USERS_EDIT_SELF to edit your own account - except a must_change_password-flagged account editing itself, which needs neither permission (issue #514): the flag alone authorizes it to change its own password, with the correct current_password, and nothing else in the same request. On this flagged path only, an omitted username, first_name, last_name or picture_file_name defaults to its stored value - the 403 refusal below is about a field that is present and different, not about which fields happen to be sent at all, so a request that sends only the new password and current_password (what this same route's own 403 body, when the flag is still set, recommends) is exactly as valid as one that resubmits every field unchanged. A flagged self-edit that sends no new password, or its current password again, is refused with 400 before anything else is checked. One that does send a new password but also sends a username, first_name, last_name or picture_file_name that differs from what is stored is refused with 403, the same answer a missing permission gets - this is an authorization refusal, not a data one, and applies whether or not a current password was also supplied.

Changing your own password - flagged or not - additionally requires the current one, sent as current_password (or current_password_base64). A password change that succeeds revokes every other session already open on the account (issue #513): when the account being changed is also the acting one and was not flagged, the session that made the request is spared; when it was flagged, every session on the account is revoked, including the one that made the request, and a freshly minted session cookie replaces it.

schema.description: amount is required. Every other property is optional: a property whose key is absent from the body keeps the entry's current value, resolved against the entry as it is at the moment of the edit rather than as it was when the request was formed. A property that is present must be readable as the type documented below, or as the additional numeric-string forms price and shopping_location_id's own descriptions name, or the request is refused with 400 and nothing about the entry changes. price, shopping_location_id and note additionally accept an explicit null to clear the field, since an absent key keeps it instead; price and shopping_location_id also accept "" for the same reason - for shopping_location_id this matches the web form's own "no store" option. best_before_date, location_id, purchased_date and open are not nullable.

amount.description: The entry's new amount. A negative amount is refused; zero is unaffected by that check.

best_before_date.description: The due date of this stock entry. Omitted keeps the entry's current due date.

price.description: The price per stock quantity unit in configured currency. Omitted keeps the entry's current price; null or "" clears it. Also accepts any string PHP's is_numeric() reads, such as "3", "2.50", "1e3", ".5" or one with leading/trailing whitespace - undocumented in the type above, matching this fork's own convention for the same field on POST /stock/products/{productId}/add and the other stock-booking routes, whose examples show it.

open.description: Whether the stock entry is opened. Also accepted: 0/1 and the strings "0"/"1" - not the word strings "true"/"false". Omitted keeps the entry's current open state; opening it for the first time stamps today as its opened date.

location_id.description: Must name an existing, active location. Omitted keeps the entry's current location.

shopping_location_id.description: Must name an existing, active shopping location. Omitted keeps the entry's current shopping location; null or "" clears it. Also accepts any string PHP's filter_var(..., FILTER_VALIDATE_INT) reads, with no leading or trailing whitespace, such as "1" or "+1" - undocumented in the type above, matching this fork's own convention for location_id/shopping_location_id on the other stock-booking routes.

purchased_date.description: The date when this stock entry was purchased. Omitted keeps the entry's current purchased date.

note.description: A free-text note. Omitted keeps the entry's current note; null clears it.

GenericEntityWrite.description:
A map of the entity's writable columns. Deliberately untyped, because that is what the server implements: `POST /objects/{entity}` and `PUT /objects/{entity}/{objectId}` take whatever keys the body carries, drop the two columns the server owns (`id` and `row_created_timestamp`) plus `userfields`, which is not a column at all - GetObject()/GetObjects() attach it to every read response, and a client that PUTs it back no longer fails on it (see GenericEntityApiController::WithoutServerOwnedColumns), and `PUT` writes only the keys present, so a partial body is a partial update. Nothing validates the body against a schema.

These two bodies used to be documented as the same undiscriminated `oneOf` the read response used. That was never accurate - the union was matched by declaration order so every entity's body was really a `Product`, and both of `Product`'s server-owned properties were documented as settable. Once the read union's members gained `required` properties for issue #232, continuing to share them would have meant documenting `id` as mandatory on a create and forcing a read-modify-write for every partial update. The column vocabulary to use here is the schema of the entity being written - Product, Chore, Battery, Location, QuantityUnit, ShoppingListItem, StockEntry, ProductBarcode, Userfield - minus `id`, `row_created_timestamp` and `userfields`.

query.name: query[]
query.description:
An array of filter conditions, each of them is a string in the form of `` where
`` is a valid field name
`` is a comparison operator, one of
  `=` equal
  `!=` not equal
  `~` contains, case insensitive for ASCII
  `!~` does not contain, case insensitive for ASCII
  `<` less
  `>` greater
  `<=` less or equal
  `>=` greater or equal
  `§` regular expression, case sensitive
`` is the value to search for

`~`, `!~` and `§` need a text field and are answered `400` on any other type, including timestamps - substring matching a timestamp would mean rendering it to a string, and the two storage engines do not render one the same way.

Case folding for `~`/`!~` is guaranteed for ASCII only. Beyond ASCII it depends on the storage engine: SQLite folds nothing outside A-Z, while PostgreSQL folds according to the database collation, so a pattern such as `æ` may additionally match `Æ` there.

A field named in `query` or `order` that the entity does not have is answered `400`.
